messages:
alex_w: Quick ask — I'm changing the Gateway TLS wiring for the inference-gateway to reference a cert we keep in infra-certs namespace instead of copying it into each env namespace. plan shows a SecretBinding ref like:

```
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1alpha2
kind: TLSCertificate
metadata:
  name: inference-cert-ref
spec:
  secretRef:
    name: inference-tls
    namespace: infra-certs
```

Will that break healthchecks or the NodePort -> NLB probe mapping? current setup has targetPort: 8443 and externalTrafficPolicy: Local. Thoughts? :thinking:

maria_s: short answer: Gateway API Secret/Cert refs generally need the secret accessible to the proxy implementation. If the gateway controller expects the secret in the gateway's namespace you'll hit a permission/lookup failure. Which controller are you using (contour, istio-gateway-api, aws-gateway-controller)?

alex_w: aws-gateway-controller. plan shows it accepted the TLSCertificate above but on apply the gateway reports TLS secret not found. I think controller looks in the gateway namespace, not the referenced namespace. I wanted to avoid copying certs across clusters/envs.

chris_r: yeah aws-gateway-controller currently resolves secrets only in gateway namespace AFAIK. Two options: (1) create a SecretBinding-like resource (controller-specific) or (2) create a ClusterSecret (we don't have one) or (3) put a lightweight Secret in the gateway ns referencing an IAM cert ARN via cert-manager.

alex_w: option 1 sounds promising — any examples? I couldn't find clear docs.

maria_s: for aws-gw we use a certmanager Certificate in infra-certs and a small Secret copy into the gateway namespace via a kustomize generator in infra repo. generator is a simple secretGenerator that uses the cert-manager produced secret as input; incase of rotation we reconcile. This keeps automation simple and avoids controller limitations.

kevin_p: fwiw, copying secrets -> watch rotation complexity. If you do that, ensure you add an annotation so our rotate-job picks it up: `redwood.com/rotate-source: infra-certs/inference-tls`

alex_w: good call. I'll add the annotation. still worried about probes: when we copy the secret and keep externalTrafficPolicy: Local, NLB healthcheck still hits nodeport 8443 -> pod 8443 but we have an envoy sidecar listening 15001 and doing TLS passthrough to the container. Any gotchas?

chris_r: two things to watch: (a) NLB expects the target port to be the pod port (or nodeport). If envoy does TLS terminate or intercept, make sure the readiness probe targets the right container port. (b) For TLS passthrough you can't terminate on ALB, NLB passthrough preserves SNI but the probe will be a TCP healthcheck hitting the nodeport. If your readiness probe is an HTTP(S) check over TLS, NLB might not do SNI — so use TCP or set up a dedicated health endpoint that returns 200 over plain HTTP on a non-TLS port.

maria_s: our pattern: keep Liveness/Readiness on plain HTTP on 15020 (non-TLS) proxied locally by envoy to the container health endpoint. Service maps targetPort -> 15020 for kube probe but NLB still points at 8443 for external TLS. So two different ports: probe->15020 internal, traffic->8443 external. That avoids TLS mismatch.

alex_w: ah that makes sense. Right now our kube readiness is pointing at 8443 which is TLS and failing the NLB probe -> we saw 502s. I'll flip readiness to the non-TLS probe and update the service targetPort mapping.

infra-bot: terraform plan finished for //modules/gateway: no resource changes except `kubernetes_secret.generated` will be added in namespace `staging-gateway` (planned).

kevin_p: thanks infra-bot. Alex, when you push the change can you include a small terraform var that toggles `copy_cert=true` so we can rollback to the copy model quickly if anything flaps?

alex_w: will do. Plan for changes:
- add secretGenerator kustomize entry that copies `infra-certs/inference-tls` -> `staging-gateway/inference-tls`
- annotate copied secret with `redwood.com/rotate-source`
- change readinessProbe to http GET on :15020/ready (non-TLS)
- keep service external port 443 -> targetPort 8443 for TLS traffic, but ensure envoy passthrough logic routes to app after TLS term if needed

maria_s: also add a note in the gateway README about why secret copy exists (controller limitation) so future folks don't delete it thinking it's redundant.

chris_r: if you want I'll review the kustomize generator PR. Also run a small canary (2 pods) before rolling across the fleet.

alex_w: thanks — I'll open PR in infra repo, tag @chris_r and @maria_s. aiming to deploy to staging by EOD. :thumbsup:
